the new z0h schemes are more appropriate than the original one for simulating surface heat fluxes, Tsfc and soil temperature in the high-altitude regions during monsoon season.
the Noah model with newly developed schemes for z0m and the z0h schemes that are more physically based can be used for the simulation of the land surface processes in high-altitude regions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the newly developed schemes can be used to improve the Noah model performance for high-altitude areas, and the z0h scheme is more important than the z0m scheme to improve the Noah simulated heat fluxes and Tsfc.

the Noah model can produce reliable estimates of the surface heat fluxes for the Tibetan Plateau if the z0m scheme is properly parameterized and if the z0h scheme is properly parameterizing diurnal variability of z0h.

the Noah model with the newly developed z0m and improved z0h schemes can be used with confidence to study the surface energy budget over high-altitude regions.
